lossBoundaries.statement: No user may gain access they were not entitled to without explicit, reviewable rationale and evidence.
Equipment must not remain in service when local condition is materially unknown.
No revenue recognition without required completion evidence or policy-approved substitute evidence.
Restart must not rely on components already beyond tolerated wear margin.
Commitments must not bypass delegated approval authority outside a documented emergency path.

decisionPatterns.title: Missing critical evidence blocks acceptance even when surrounding signals look healthy
decisionPatterns.applicableContext: Cases where a key risk boundary depends on evidence that is absent, stale, or bypassed despite surrounding signs of normality or urgency.
acceptanceConditions: A policy-approved substitute evidence path exists and is documented.
evidenceRequired: Primary evidence for the gated decision or explicit approved substitute
exceptions: Conditionally acceptable only through documented waiver authority and compensating controls.

includedContexts: review or approval depends on evidence that protects a defined loss boundary
missing evidence changes risk, not just convenience
excludedContexts: cases where equivalent substitute evidence is already explicitly approved
assumptions: Loss boundary is explicit enough to judge.
Evaluator can inspect allowed evidence types.
invalidationSignals: context no longer exposes the same harm mode

qualityIntentDerivations.derivedIntentStatement: Acceptance decisions must be grounded in evidence that explicitly protects the relevant loss boundary; normal-looking surrounding signals are not sufficient substitutes.
qualityIntentDerivations.rationale: Across domains, experts rejected or constrained decisions when key protective evidence was missing, stale, or bypassed.

failureAnalysis: One evaluator initially over-generalized the pattern to reject all missing-approval cases, then corrected after reading the waiver path.

organizationalQualityCultures.name: Boundary-protective quality culture
preferredEvidence: Primary evidence close to the boundary
explicit waiver records when exceptions are used
organizationalQualityCultures.riskAppetite: Conservative on irreversible harm, conditional on administrative urgency when waiver authority is explicit.
escalationNorms: Escalate when key evidence is missing but pressure is high.
Escalate when local state is unknown.
Escalate when authority bypass is proposed.
waiverPractices: Waivers are allowed only through named authority and retrospective audit.
qualityTradeoffs: Speed is secondary to boundary protection.
Urgency can modify route but not erase evidence needs.
subgroupDifferences: Administration tolerates emergency paths more than software security does.

reviewHistoryInferences.inferredPatternSummary: Comments repeatedly block acceptance when protective evidence is absent despite apparently normal progress signals.

governanceEvents.reason: Cross-domain expert judgments revealed a stable protective pattern around missing critical evidence.
governanceEvents.decision: Validated for baseline use with bounded applicability.

criteria.statement: Every validated pattern cites cues, concern, loss boundary, source judgments, and reproduction test.
